comparison: Both support the behavioral findings of similarity masking (C6, C7, C14). OpenEval provides more detailed analysis including reaction time patterns (C15-C18), while peer reviewers accept behavioral data without detailed discussion of RT findings. Both note consistency with human psychophysical results.

OpenEval R1 includes reaction time claims (C15-C18) that peer R4 accepts implicitly as part of the overall behavioral characterization without explicit discussion. Both evaluations support these findings, though peer review provides less detailed commentary.

Strong agreement on biphasic VSDI dynamics (C8, C9, C10, C11). Both explicitly recognize this as a key contribution. OpenEval includes C58 (correct-trial analysis) which peer R12 addresses separately. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED with similar enthusiasm for the findings.

Strong agreement on columnar vs retinotopic scale findings (C22, C23, C24). Peer reviewer explicitly praises this as a strength. Both support the novelty claim (C25), though OpenEval notes this depends on literature knowledge while peer reviewers do not challenge it.

Perfect claim overlap (C12, C28-C32) on population vector dynamics. Both support the findings. OpenEval notes the tilt illusion connection (C30) is speculative, while peer reviewers implicitly accept the population dynamics without detailed critique of this specific speculation.

Strong agreement on modeling results (C33-C36, C4). Both support the model as providing a reasonable qualitative account. OpenEval notes C38 (V1 origins) needs more evidence; peer R7 addresses this interpretive claim separately with UNCERTAIN evaluation due to center vs surround debate.

Both address overarching conclusions about V1's role (C5, C13). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on convergent evidence. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN due to significant debate about center vs surround mechanisms, with Reviewer 2 challenging the interpretation despite accepting the data.

Perfect claim overlap (C26, C27). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN noting the RT explanation is speculative and needs additional experiments. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, accepting the claims as following logically from biphasic dynamics. This represents a notable disagreement in evaluation stringency.

Perfect claim overlap (C39-C42) on center-surround interaction claims. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with caveats about limited experimental testing. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN with Reviewer 2 directly challenging the interpretation and calling for additional experiments. Significant disagreement on evidential sufficiency.

Perfect claim overlap (C43-C47) on theoretical framework about natural vision. Both rate SUPPORTED. Both recognize these as theoretical interpretations appropriately supported by citations rather than direct experimental findings. Strong agreement.

Both address response reduction claims (C20, C21). OpenEval notes the mechanistic interpretation is speculative given later complex analyses. Peer reviewers accept the observation without challenge, noting appropriate qualification. Both SUPPORTED with similar caveats.

OpenEval R10 includes C19 (responses at both spatial scales) which peer R3 also references as part of the spatial scale analysis. Both support these observations, though they are grouped differently in the two evaluations.

OpenEval R11 addresses methodological claims (C48-C57) while peer R12 addresses control analyses (C58-C60). Both support the quality of methods and controls. OpenEval provides more detailed methodological assessment while peer review focuses on experimental design quality.

Both address generalizability claims (C59, C60). Both rate SUPPORTED while acknowledging incomplete data across all conditions. OpenEval notes more complete data would strengthen claims; peer reviewers accept the work as 'well done' and 'thoughtfully designed.'

OpenEval evaluates foundational prior knowledge claim (C1) about similarity masking as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers do not explicitly assess this background claim.

OpenEval evaluates established knowledge about V1 orientation selectivity (C37) as SUPPORTED. Peer R7 includes C37 in discussion of V1 origins but focuses on the interpretive debate rather than evaluating this established fact separately.

OpenEval R2 includes C58 (correct-trial analysis) as supporting evidence for biphasic dynamics. Peer R12 addresses this as part of control analyses. Both support the validity of this control, though grouped in different evaluation contexts.
